result.rule: Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
An ordinary embedded subprocess participates in normal sequence flow and may contain its own starts, ends, activities, gateways and flows.
Use lanes to partition one process by a stated role, department, system or responsibility; lanes are not separate processes.

Give every process and every expanded subProcess its own explicit start event and end event. A trigger that occurs after the main flow (for example later feedback or a return) is joined to the main flow by a gateway, or modeled as an event subprocess or a separate process.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.

result.rule: When the description names multiple required activities in a phase, gives no order among them, and states that a later outcome occurs only after the phase is finished: Model each activity separately, use a parallel split for the unordered activities, and join their branches before modeling the later outcome.

When the description states that work proceeds concurrently and that a later step must wait until all of that work is complete: Model the concurrent work as parallel branches and synchronize them with a parallel gateway before the dependent step.

When the description says that one of several alternatives is selected, or that an activity may occur: Model the choice or optional activity with an appropriate gateway, and reconnect the resulting paths before subsequent common work.

When the description identifies distinct participants and describes information or items being communicated or handed off between them: Model each participant as a separate pool and represent each described exchange between participants with a message flow from sender to receiver, using valid interaction nodes.
